History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
• 23-year-old woman developed rapidly progressive upper-lip swelling, breathing difficulty, and dizziness ~30 min after eating prawn soup; clinician arranged emergency ambulance for suspected anaphylaxis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden swelling of left upper lip spreading across upper lip after ingestion of prawn soup at ~19:00 today.  
• Timeline: 
  – Ate prawn soup ≈19:00.  
  – Noticed tingling/swelling at left corner of lip within ~30 min.  
  – Swelling has continued to enlarge; feels “pumping” sensation.  
• Associated symptoms: Difficulty breathing, possible chest tightness, dizziness. Denies/No data on rash, GI upset, or loss of consciousness.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: No relief measures taken prior to call.  
• Relevant past similar episode: One year ago after late-night Chinese meal; awoke next morning with generalized swelling and breathing difficulty; self-treated only with salbutamol inhaler.  
• Review of systems: Limited by urgency; positives noted above, no additional systems discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – uses salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no maintenance inhaler.  
• Peanut allergy – history of severe reaction requiring hospital treatment with injection at age 6.  
• Prior possible food-triggered allergic reaction one year ago (details above).
Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Intermittent antihistamines for peanut allergy – name/dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Peanuts – documented severe allergy.  
• Shellfish allergy suspected (first reaction today; not previously diagnosed).

Social History:
• Lives with mother (present at home).  
• Socializes with friends; occasional alcohol (was “quite drunk” during prior episode).  
• No information provided on smoking or recreational drug use.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Remote video; no formal vitals or exam performed.  
• Patient-reported findings: visibly swollen upper lip; subjective breathing difficulty; dizziness.

Investigations:
• None obtained during teleconsult.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1 – Suspected anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn):
  • Assessment: Acute oropharyngeal angio-edema with respiratory compromise after shellfish exposure; high likelihood of anaphylaxis.
  • Plan:
    – Immediate 999 ambulance activation (completed during call).  
    – Instructed patient to take available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
    – Advised continuous supervision until ambulance arrival.  
    – Anticipate emergency department management with intramuscular epinephrine, airway support, steroids, antihistamines, observation.

Issue 2 – Food allergies (peanut and probable shellfish):
  • Assessment: History of severe peanut allergy; new likely shellfish allergy.
  • Plan (post-discharge):
    – Arrange follow-up for formal allergy testing/confirmation.  
    – Prescribe/educate on carrying epinephrine auto-injector(s).  
    – Provide written emergency action plan and avoidance counseling.

Issue 3 – Asthma:
  • Assessment: Known asthma; currently using only salbutamol inhaler.
  • Plan (post-discharge):
    – Review asthma control; consider initiating maintenance inhaler (e.g., inhaled corticosteroid).  
    – Reinforce inhaler technique and provide asthma action plan.

General:
• Advise return video/clinic appointment after hospital discharge for medication reconciliation, allergy kit issuance, and chronic care review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: Vital signs, full drug/allergy list, current medication doses, past surgical history, comprehensive ROS, family history, immunization status.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audible recording; limited data due to emergency nature.
